calls.title: Ryanair Enterprise Trial - GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team is actively working on a $220,000 UK-based financial trial, aiming to align efforts with contract renewals occurring in August-September 2024. Scott Keller emphasized the importance of migration planning for 100 experiments and feature flags, with Liam set to lead after a handover from Pat Lee. However, there are concerns regarding limited user engagement on the internal trial platform, Retool, prompting Logan Bates to investigate analytics capabilities. Proactive customer communication is being prioritized to avoid stagnation in trial usage, alongside a structured leadership transition to ensure continuity in managing key accounts. The urgency to improve trial tracking and customer interactions is critical to closing upcoming contracts and enhancing customer satisfaction.
calls.keywords: POC success plan, Retool usage, Lead water line replacement, UK financial client, Contract renewal, Migration effort
calls.action_items:
**Scott Keller**
Send a ping and follow-up email to the client regarding the updated POC success plan and meeting time correction to ensure acceptance (03:10)
Monitor Retool license activity and connection status, addressing any lack of usage or engagement (02:52)
Reschedule missed meetings with the UK financial client to maintain engagement before their contract renewal period (09:56)

**Logan Bates**
Review the POC success plan shared by Scott to provide feedback or follow-up (01:33)
Investigate Retool platform capabilities on user login tracking to better assess client engagement (01:49)
Assist Scott once his water issue is resolved or if additional help is needed (08:11)

calls.title: Ryanair / GrowthBook Reconnect
calls.summary: The team is working on modernizing the payment platform to include localized payment methods that cater specifically to European markets. This initiative, led by Paul Sheridan, emphasizes the importance of integrating country-specific payment preferences, although progress is hindered due to resource constraints and communication challenges, particularly with network restrictions blocking Slack usage. Additionally, the import of feature flags from LaunchDarkly has revealed potential issues related to licensing, requiring further investigation to ensure efficient deployment. Dedicated support has been arranged to assist during the migration process, while contract renewals for LaunchDarkly and Optimizely are on the horizon, emphasizing the need for proactive planning aligned with project milestones.
calls.keywords: Payment platform, feature flags, LaunchDarkly, Enterprise trial, Slack integration, Optimizely
calls.action_items:
**Scott Keller**
Extend Ryanair’s Enterprise trial license and send confirmation to Paul Sheridan (09:37)
Follow up on the Teams-Slack integration invite to Ryanair and coordinate with their security team to enable external invites if possible (07:24)
Assist Logan Bates in debugging the LaunchDarkly import issues and project flag assignment problems (09:43)

**Logan Bates**
Investigate why feature flags are missing from specific projects after import and determine if this is related to project licensing or technical glitches (10:54)
Explore supporting Optimizely data import using agents like Clotter and provide related support to Ryanair (09:56)
Encourage Paul Sheridan to share detailed import data via email to aid debugging of import and flag issues (09:43)

Complete current development tasks within a week to enable further testing by returning colleague (07:44)
